residue.text: Preserved stage1 rival H2 and INV concern: unrelated traffic or volunteer redistribution may produce recovery. INV additionally hypothesizes that reporting a shortage triggers searching and supplementation, reversing the proposed causal arrow. Record report, search, and transfer order; an unwatched mat counter remains unattributed even after restoring twelve.

Preserved H3: historical starting and return counts lacked independent checks. Disagreement without movement retains counting uncertainty; agreed checkout twelve followed by agreed return eleven weakens pure counting error for that event, but agreement can share error.

Preserved ATT alternative hypothesis: replace self-service return with attended checkout-table handback, keeping numbered trays and full allowances. One volunteer watches placement while the other counts. This sacrifices unattended return and may create queues; feasibility and outcome preservation are untested. Retain it as an alternative requiring its own bounded selection, not an additional block.

Preserved limits: historical six loans per block do not fix future demand. Predeclare the intended schedule and record deviations. Tray-specific shortages and closing concentration establish no cause; every tray also had a complete return. Small samples may show no anomaly, and changed attention or compliance confounds improvement. Counter location, closing-time cause, queue feasibility, and the meaning of available kits remain unresolved.

summary.text: Retain stage1 H1 as the provisional working hypothesis: borrower completion may follow tray placement. The stipulated recoveries and timing fit it but establish neither origin nor cause; the fourth shortage remains unresolved.

Candidate construction: retain numbered open trays and self-service shelf, routing loose counters into the corresponding tray. Following INV, prospectively select sequential ordinary and intervention returns under the same planned demand. Hypothesis H1 predicts a watched corresponding borrower arrival before an agreed rise from eleven to twelve; H2 predicts unrelated transfers. Withhold undocumented supplementation until timed counts are recorded. Improvement alone identifies no cause.

Use one twenty-minute block, two volunteers, forty person-minutes, and at most one inspected tray. Record separate checkout and initial return counts before sharing results, seconds and transfer order, later tray/mat counts at one, three, and five minutes when feasible, active loans, waiting borrowers, and remaining time. Record disagreements before recounting.

Seventy-one accounted counters permit five complete kits plus eleven counters, subject to verification. Issue exactly twelve; preserve five-minute use and active loans. Log replenishment separately from borrower-return evidence. Five circulating kits do not guarantee five ready shelf kits. An unresolved five-minute shortage or block-end truncation fails to demonstrate reconciliation; no intervention success is established.
